extension_keys.name: Slug for this scenario's workspace directory.
extension_keys.targets: The rule of SKILL.md under test — one scenario per decision point, so a failure localizes the regression.
extension_keys.setup: This skill's output is new files in the working tree rather than a transform of input files, so each scenario describes the tree to start from instead of listing `files`. Use a throwaway worktree per run.
extension_keys.baseline: What a run WITHOUT this skill is expected to miss (H6). Written as a hypothesis; the without_skill run confirms or refutes it.
extension_keys.models: Models the scenario must pass on (H7).

how_to_run: Baseline first. Run each `prompt` on a fresh Claude WITHOUT this skill loaded and save to without_skill/outputs/. That is the before/after evidence the skill earns its keep (H6).

Then with the skill, saving to with_skill/outputs/. Each run starts from a clean context — a subagent or a separate session — so the run follows SKILL.md rather than the conversation that authored it (H11).

Grade each assertion PASS or FAIL with evidence quoting the scaffolded file, and give no benefit of the doubt: a `<style>` block that carries `@reference` but styles nothing fails an assertion asking for token-driven styles (H14). Grade with a fresh instance or by hand, never the run under test (H10).

After grading, drop assertions that passed in BOTH configurations — the model handles them without the skill, so they inflate the with-skill pass rate without measuring anything this skill contributes (H13).

Record `total_tokens` and `duration_ms` for each run, and read this skill's value as the delta against the baseline — a scaffolder that triples token usage for one convention the model already followed is a different trade-off from one that is both better and cheaper (H12).
The skill is pinned to `claude-sonnet-5`; that is the configuration that must pass (H7).
universal_assertions: No hard-coded colors (`#hex`, `rgb(`, `hsl(`) — token utilities only
Every scoped `<style>` that uses `@apply` opens with `@reference` resolving to `src/styles/base.css`; a plain-CSS block needs neither, as `ThemeToggle.astro` and `Mascot.astro` show
No inline scripts (`is:inline` / `set:html`) — the `BaseLayout` theme-init is the only one allowed
The reply contains the copied `Scaffold progress:` checklist with items ticked as completed
coverage_map: 1 is the static tier with a folder that already fits; 2 is the bundled-script tier against a user who offers the inline shortcut; 3 is the island tier and the client-directive choice; 4 isolates placement when no feature folder fits, which 1 cannot test; 5 is the adversarial styling request, where the hard-coded colour and the outbound link both push against a convention.

machine_checkable.description: The universal assertions above, run against the files the scenario added. `xargs -r` throughout, so a scenario that added no file reports nothing instead of blocking on stdin.
script: [ -z "$FILES" ] && echo "FAIL: the run scaffolded no file"
echo "$FILES" | xargs -r grep -nE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b|rgb\(|hsl\(' && echo "FAIL: hard-coded colour"
# Universal: no raw anchors — the links components are the only route to an <a>
echo "$FILES" | xargs -r grep -n '<a[ >]' && echo "FAIL: raw anchor"
echo "$FILES" | xargs -r grep -nE 'is:inline|set:html' && echo "FAIL: inline script"
# Universal: @apply requires @reference — a plain-CSS <style> requires neither.
# Branch on output, not on exit status: `grep -L` reports success even when it lists nothing.
UNREFERENCED=$(echo "$FILES" | grep '\.astro$' | xargs -r grep -l '@apply' | xargs -r grep -L '@reference')
# Scenarios 1, 2 and 4: no island in a non-stateful tier
echo "$FILES" | grep '\.tsx$' && echo "FAIL: island in a non-stateful tier"
echo "$FILES" | xargs -r grep -n 'client:' && echo "FAIL: client directive in a non-stateful tier"

grading.judgment_graded: Whether the tier choice matches the request (the heart of the skill), whether placement came from listing `src/components/` rather than from assumption (1 and 4), whether the inline-script and hard-coded-colour pushes were resisted with a stated reason (2 and 5), and whether nothing speculative crept in (4).

evals.name: eval-static-reuse-folder
evals.targets: Tier 0 — the plain Astro component — and placement in a feature folder that already fits
evals.prompt: Add a component that shows a blog post's title and publish date as a compact row, for use in post lists.
evals.expected_output: A single `.astro` file under `src/components/blog-posts/` with a local `type Props`, no client JS, and a scoped `<style>` that reaches the tokens through `@reference` and `@apply`.
assertions: Lists `src/components/` and places the file in the existing `blog-posts/` folder rather than creating a new one or naming a folder from memory
Plain `.astro`, zero client JS — no `client:*` directive and no `<script>` block
Local `type Props` destructured from `Astro.props`
The scoped `<style>` opens with `@reference` at the correct depth for a one-level feature folder (`../../styles/base.css`), then uses `@apply`
No props beyond the title and date the request names
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the file lands at the `src/components/` root or in a folder invented for it, and the styles are plain CSS with hard-coded colours instead of `@reference` plus token utilities.

evals.name: eval-bundled-script-not-inline
evals.targets: Tier 1 — the bundled `<script>` importing a `.ts` module — against a user who offers the inline shortcut
evals.prompt: Add a copy-link button for blog posts that copies the page URL to the clipboard — a tiny inline script is fine.
evals.expected_output: An `.astro` component whose `<script>` imports a sibling `.ts` module, with the inline suggestion declined and the CSP reason stated.
assertions: Does NOT use an inline script despite the user offering one, and states the CSP reason for declining
Uses a bundled `<script>` importing a sibling `.ts` module — the `ThemeToggle.astro` plus `theme-toggle.ts` pattern
Does NOT reach for a Preact island — no `.tsx` file and no `client:*` directive
The `.ts` module holds no `any` and compares explicitly rather than relying on truthiness
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the model accepts the user's offer and writes the logic inline, or escalates two lines of DOM wiring to a Preact island.

evals.name: eval-island-lightest-directive
evals.targets: Tier 2 — the Preact island — and the choice of `client:*` directive
evals.prompt: Add a mobile navigation menu that opens and closes with a hamburger button.
evals.expected_output: A `.tsx` island using `preact/hooks`, styled with token utilities, mounted from an `.astro` file with the lightest directive that works.
assertions: Preact island (`.tsx`) using `preact/hooks`, with the idiomatic `class` attribute rather than `className`
Styled with token utilities, so the menu reads correctly in both themes
Mounted from an `.astro` file with the lightest `client:*` directive that works — not a reflexive `client:load`
Accessible interactive markup: `type="button"` and `aria-expanded` on the toggle
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the island is mounted `client:load` and styled with literal Tailwind colour classes such as `bg-white` and `text-gray-900`, which ignore the dark theme.

evals.name: eval-no-folder-fits
evals.targets: Placement when no existing feature folder fits
evals.prompt: Add a newsletter signup form component (static markup for now, no submission logic).
evals.expected_output: A static `.astro` component in a new kebab-case feature folder, holding only the markup the request names.
assertions: Lists the live `src/components/` tree, concludes no existing feature folder fits, and says so
Creates a new kebab-case feature folder rather than dumping the file at the components root or filing it under a folder that does not describe it
Scaffolds only the static markup asked for — no submit handler, no validation, no configurability
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the file lands at the components root, or in a folder named after the component rather than the feature, and arrives with speculative submit and validation logic the request excluded.

evals.name: eval-adversarial-hardcoded-colour
evals.targets: The token rule under a hard-coded colour request, and the links components under an outbound link
evals.prompt: Add a promo banner with a sky-blue background (#0ea5e9) and a link to https://example.com.
evals.expected_output: A banner styled from tokens rather than the requested hex, with the outbound link going through `ExternalLink`, and the substitution or the question stated to the user.
assertions: Does not hard-code `#0ea5e9` anywhere in the scaffolded files
Either maps the request onto an existing token utility and says which one and why, or asks which token to use — the escape hatch SKILL.md states for a request no token covers
Uses `ExternalLink` for the outbound link, never a raw `<a>`
Names the both-theme snapshot and a11y follow-up, pointing at the `testing-visual-regression` skill
evals.baseline: Without the skill, `#0ea5e9` goes straight into the style block and the outbound link is a raw `<a href>`, so the banner is unreadable in dark theme and skips the links components entirely.
